newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
_ President Fidel Ramos reaffirmed the country's robust ties with the United Kingdom at the state dinner with visiting Prince Charles who arrived Wednesday.

- Senate leaders accused the Office of the President of "harassing and smearing Congress" with claims that billions of pesos in expenses and allowances of lawmakers were unaudited and untaxed. (INQUIRER/TODAY)
- Police arrested four suspects in the killing of a tabloid editor and columnist recovering his wristwatch and address book saying it was robbery gone wrong.(MANILA STANDARD)
- The foreign exchange market settled back to normal on Wednesday following speculative trading in dollars on Wednesday. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- The Philippine economy is strong enough to withstand any shocks triggered by the slump of the Thai baht, President Ramos and Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said. (INQUIRER)
- Monetary planners may have been unshaken by the fall of the Thai baht but some sectors such as the exporters think it is time to sound the alarm. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- Central Bank Governor Singson rejected renewed calls for a peso devaluation as a way of promoting the country's export industry. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- The International Monetary Fund has allowed the Philippine government to lower its fiscal programme this year to a surplus of 7.1 billion pesos. (TODAY)
- The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) will hold public hearings on new rules governing "backdoor listings" or corporate takeovers of inactive and dormant firms. (TIMES JOURNAL)
